issue_context.title: Document how to use search_after w/ a point in time (PIT) via HLRC
issue_context.body:
In modern versions of Elasticsearch, the recommended approach for deep pagination is to use `search_after` [1] with a point in time (PIT) [2].

It'd be helpful to document how to perform this type of search/pagination with the HLRC.

[1] https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.11/paginate-search-results.html#search-after
[2] https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/7.11/point-in-time-api.html

review_comments: It is good to add `OpenPointInTimeResponseTests` to check serialization from and to XContent. But I don't mind if we do it in a following PR.
Can you please explain what's the need for this change?

This is a bit messy. ClosePointInTimeResponse extends ClearScrollResponse, and this change just ensures that `fromXContent` method returns an instance of ClosePointInTimeResponse. I will work on a small PR to clean up this.

I was thinking that open and delete PIT APIs should return almost instantly,  thus is there a need for `openPointInTimeAsync`  and `closePointInTimeAsync` ?  Or, am I wrong, and there are cases when these APIs may take some time?
Yes, it should be fast unless the request hits many indices or the cluster is not functioning. But here I merely follow the convention in HLRC that is returning Cancellable in *Async methods.
